title: Team
text:
Jean-Christophe Boucher is an Associate Professor at the Department of Political Science at the University of Calgary. His current work focuses on applying machine learning to understand how the digital world shapes society, particularly in the context of foreign information manipulation and interference. He is a Fulbright Scholar and manages projects funded by the Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council (SSHRC) and the Department of National Defence. In 2025, he served as Deputy Director - Data Science within the Rapid Response Mechanism (RRM) at Global Affairs Canada. He specializes in international relations, with a focus on foreign policy, global security, and data analytics.
Jean-Christophe Boucher est professeur associé au département de sciences politiques de l’université de Calgary. Ses travaux actuels portent sur l’application de l’apprentissage automatique pour comprendre comment le monde numérique façonne la société, notamment en ce qui concerne la manipulation de l’information et l’interférence étrangère. Il est titulaire d’une bourse Fulbright et est actuellement responsable de projets financés par le Conseil de recherches en sciences humaines (CRSH) et la défense nationale. En 2025, il a occupé le poste de directeur adjoint – Science des données au sein du Mécanisme de réponse rapide (RRM) d’Affaires mondiales Canada. Il est spécialisé dans l’analyse de la politique étrangère, la sécurité internationale et l’analyse de données.

title: Team
text:
Research Team Leads







Israa Farouk
Israa Farouk is the Team Lead on Computer Science, bringing her expertise in data science and analytics to support the group’s research. She earned her Master’s degree in Data Science and Analytics from the University of Calgary, where her work focused on applying statistical and machine learning techniques to complex datasets.
Israa supports evidence-based research by applying data analysis and visualization techniques to inform policy development. She is passionate about using innovative analytical approaches to promote sustainable practices and inform evidence-based decision-making.










David Dubé
David Dubé is a PhD Candidate in Political Science at McGill University and the Research Team Lead for the Information Security and Influence Team, which he joined in October 2022. His research examines how state actors exploit digital information ecosystems to promote strategic narratives, influence political interpretation, and contest international order. This work is especially concerned with the measurement and detection of misinformation, foreign influence, and inauthentic or synthetic content across digital platforms.
Through past experience as a Senior Data Analyst with Global Affairs Canada’s Rapid Response Mechanism, David leads applied research and analytical work on foreign information manipulation targeting Canada and its allies. Methodologically, he combines qualitative, quantitative, and computational approaches, including natural language processing, machine learning, and large-scale text analysis, applied to comparative political economy and the study of disinformation strategies employed by authoritarian and great-power states.
David holds a Master’s degree in Political Science and International Relations from the University of Quebec at Montréal, where he wrote his thesis on the construction of Russia’s revanchist identity and the annexation of Crimea.

title: The Societal Defence Lab
text:
The Societal Defence Lab conducts research on total defence, examining the societal foundations that sustain national defence and the hybrid campaigns that target them. Combining survey experimentation on civil-military relations and public trust in the armed forces with computational analysis of foreign information manipulation, the Lab produces evidence on how democratic societies absorb coercive pressure below the threshold of armed conflict.

What We Do
Our research is organized around two complementary teams, united by a shared interest in how public trust underpins — and is targeted to undermine — national defence.
Information Security and Influence Team
This team examines hybrid conflict and foreign information manipulation, building the Lab’s own AI systems to do so. Our engineering team develops multilingual analysis pipelines, custom classification and detection models, and measurement infrastructure capable of operating at scale across global information environments, functioning as much as a development shop as a research group, since these questions cannot be answered with off-the-shelf tooling.
Defense and Foreign Policy Team
This team examines civil-military relations and public trust in the armed forces, since consent, legitimacy, and effective civilian oversight determine whether defence institutions can act at all. Through survey and survey-experimental research, they measure how societies understand and support their defence institutions across Canada, the United States, Europe, and Atlantic alliance partners.


Funding
Our work is supported by the Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council of Canada (SSHRC) and the Department of National Defence’s Mobilizing Insights in Defence and Security (MINDS) program.

2026 — SSHRC Partnership Grant (Talent) – 3CE

2026 — Agence Nationale de la Recherche – France
2025 — Department of National Defence – MINDS Network Grant
2025 — SSHRC Insight Grant – Far-Left Media Ecosystems
2023 — SSHRC Insight Grant – Swing State and World Politics



Impact
We produce research that advances the discipline theoretically and methodologically, while contributing directly to Canadian and global dialogue on information threats, security, and defence. Our findings inform both academic debate and policy practice, with work published in International Studies Quarterly, the International Journal, PNAS Nexus, Armed Forces and Society, The Journal of Intelligence, Conflict and Warfare, the Journal of Medical Internet Research, BMC Public Health and The Oxford Handbook of Foreign Policy.


Leadership
The network is directed by Jean-Christophe Boucher of the University of Calgary.

title: About
text:
The Societal Defence Lab is a research group based at the University of Calgary that studies total defence: the proposition that a society’s capacity to resist coercion rests on the whole of that society rather than on its armed forces alone. We examine the civilian foundations of national defence and the adversarial campaigns designed to erode them, combining computational text analysis, survey research, and experimental methods to study questions spanning civil-military relations, public trust in defence institutions, hybrid conflict, and foreign information manipulation.

Our Mission
The Lab is committed to multidisciplinary research that bridges political science, security studies, and computer science to address the most pressing defence and information security challenges facing Canada and its allies. We treat public trust as a defence capability in its own right — one that must be studied, measured, and defended with the same rigor applied to military capability. This means building our own AI systems and measurement infrastructure where existing tools fall short, alongside survey and experimental research on how societies understand and support their defence institutions.
We believe academic knowledge must engage beyond the university. The Lab actively takes part in academic and policy debates, interacts with civil society and government partners, and is committed to bridging the gap between academic research and public understanding — ensuring our findings are accessible and useful to the communities they concern.
